newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech financial sector share losses drag PSE down.
newsitem.headline: Czech financial sector share losses drag PSE down.

text.p: Fallout from the recent problems in the banking sector continued to wreak havoc on financial institution shares on the Prague Stock Exchange on Wednesday, pulling the bourse lower for the second consecutive session.
Banks Komercni Banka, Ceska Sporitelna, and Zivnostenska Banka all lost ground as the Reuters RPIX index eased one point to 1,141, while the broader PX50 index dropped 2.1 points to 559.6.
"There's still a little wariness over financial shares following the Agrobanka affair, but I expect that in Komercni's case, we should see it gain back a little," said one trader.

Komercni fell 17 crowns at the fixing to 2,308 and then rebounded before falling back to its early loss, though dealers noted that some investors were probaly taking some profits after the issue rose some 100 crowns over the past week of trading.
Zivnostenska shares lost nine crowns to 2,711 and Sporitelna edged five crowns lower to 333.

Financial sector shares have been hit hard recently after the failure of Kreditni Banka spilled over into other banks, causing the central bank to put Agrobanka, the fifth largest bank, into temporary forced administration.
On Tuesday, the parliament set up a commission to look into Kreditni's failure.
Other blue chips were mixed, with SPT Telecom closing up 15 crowns 3,345, CEZ gaining five crowns to 1,036, while Chemopetrol dipped 13 crowns to 1,302.
Overall volume on the day was modest at 602,860 shares on turnover of 521.6 million crowns.
